newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended an abbreviated pre-New Year holiday trading session narrowly mixed. January ended $20 higher at $1,272 per tonne, while March lost $3 to close at $1,235 per tonne. In New York arabica futures closed out the year in quiet fashion, scoring modest gains in an abbreviated pre-Holiday session. March closed 95 points higher at 116.90 cents/lb while May added 1.10 cents/lb to close at 114.75 cents/lb. The fact that US certified coffee stocks remained unchanged during the week ended December 27 should not have a significant impact on prices.

UNITED STATES - US certified coffee stocks remained unchanged 34,065 bags of which 778 bags in New York, 7,768 bags in New Orleans and 25,519 bags in Miami during the week ended December 27. There were no bags pending grading.

BRAZIL - The Brazilian goverment will auction 120,100 60- kg bags of coffee in its next monthly sale on January 8, a spokesman for the Banco do Brasil which is to hold the electronic sales said. Earlier an official from the National Coffee Department had said that the auction would be for 116,100 bags. Of the total 54,000 bags will be from Parana state, 41,751 bags from Sao Paulo state and 24,349 bags from Minas Gerais state. The coffee will be from the 1986/87 and the 1987/88 harvests.

BRAZIL - Brazil exported 7.046 million bags of coffee in April/September 1996, down from 8.067 million bags exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (April/May) reached 13.7 million bags, down from 15.8 million bags in 1994/95. The main markets for green coffee in April/September 1996 were Italy (559,100 vs 778,600 bags), the United States (1.063 vs 1.317 million bags) and Japan (605,500 vs 554,800 bags). The main markets for solubles in April/September 1996 were Russia (344,800 vs 575,800 bags) and the United States (289,800 vs 189,800 bags).

ROMANIA - Romania imported 372,600 bags of coffee in January/October 1996, 80 percent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 reached 399,700 bags. The major supplier of green coffee in January/October 1996 was Indonesia with 169,000 bags up from 27,800 bags shipped the same period in 1995.
